source_updates.title: Echo Detection Using the Herglotz Wavefunction in Spatial Room Impulse Responses Measured with Spherical Microphone Arrays
findings: Herglotz localization is followed by nonnegative spherical-Gaussian fitting and an empirically selected AIC-like echo-count criterion
the large simulation uses equal-amplitude echoes, 35-degree minimum angular separation, and 250 configurations for each echo count from 1 to 12
measured EM64 validation uses one IRCAM ESPRO configuration and ISM-computed reference directions rather than directly measured ground-truth DoAs
all methods detect the direct sound and first reflection in the 10 ms frame; MUSIC is best for direct-sound angular error while Herglotz is best for first-reflection and relative-presence errors
in one 42 ms frame with 13 later reflections, detection rates are Herglotz 70%, SRP 31%, maxWDI 62%, and MUSIC 38%
cross-frame tracking, false-positive rejection, ToA and spectral reconstruction, resynthesis, and listening quality are not validated
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Promising diagnostic for overlapping early-reflection directions in higher-order SRIRs; not evidence for an automatic reverb renderer or musical mix rule.

source_updates.title: Neural Field-of-View for Binaural Signal Matching with Wearable Microphone Arrays
findings: FoV-BSM-Net predicts a signal-dependent spatial weighting mask for binaural signal matching from a wearable microphone array
the dataset is 12000 simulated single-source speech scenes with a 9600/1200/1200 split
the NMSE contract uses full complex error below 1.5 kHz and magnitude-only error above 1.5 kHz
the MUSHRA study has 12 normal-hearing listeners and two simulated speech scenes
at low DRR adaptive FoV is not significantly different from the reference, but is also not significantly better than fixed FoV
at high DRR adaptive FoV beats fixed FoV but remains 23.7 MUSHRA points below the reference
real recordings, multiple sources, music, moving listeners and personalized HRTFs are not validated
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Research candidate for binaural reproduction from sparse wearable arrays; not evidence for conventional stereo rock-mix panning, width or spatial processing.

Neve pair or 33609-style plug-in; threshold 0, recovery 100 ms, ratio 2:1; output gain is gain staging
leave channels unlinked so a large hit on one side does not duck the opposite side

knowledge_cards.claim: Herglotz improves dense-frame direction and presence estimation in the reported SMA conditions, not reverb rendering quality.
The measured Herglotz reference directions are ISM-derived and are not independent physical ground truth.
Equal-amplitude echoes and a 35-degree minimum separation bound the large Herglotz simulation.
The empirically chosen AIC-like criterion needs false-positive and alternative-criterion checks before unattended use.
Single-frame echo detection does not solve cross-frame association, time-of-arrival or reflection reconstruction.
FoV-BSM-Net evidence is simulated, single-source and speech-based.
Magnitude-only NMSE above 1.5 kHz is a study-specific contract, not a universal music-spatial metric.
Twelve listeners and two simulated scenes support a narrow perceptual comparison, not broad music generalization.
A non-significant difference from the reference in a small test does not establish equivalence.
The high-DRR adaptive system still differs substantially from the reference despite beating fixed FoV.
CLA's unlinked parallel bus is an engineer preference whose stereo and centre behavior must be measured.
Spoken compressor and EQ values describe one chain and do not define a portable preset without processor and gain-reduction parity.

experiments.title: Linked versus unlinked parallel drum compression
experiments.variant: the same two compressor channels in dual-mono or unlinked mode
experiments.loudness_matching: retain raw safety renders; create separate integrated-loudness-matched blind copies
experiments.success: unlinked mode gives repeatable preferred width or punch without unstable centre motion, mono loss or extra peak risk
experiments.cancel: link parity cannot be established, image motion becomes distracting, centre elements shift, mono residual worsens, or preference disappears after loudness matching

experiments.title: CLA parallel-return EQ contribution
experiments.baseline: same parallel return with EQ bypassed
experiments.variant: same return with approximately +3 dB at 60 Hz and +3 dB at 8 kHz
experiments.success: EQ improves useful weight and point without masking or harshness
experiments.cancel: peak risk, low-end masking or high-frequency harshness worsens

experiments.title: Herglotz versus conventional echo-localization maps on held-out measured SRIRs
experiments.baseline: SRP, maxWDI and MUSIC with the same Gaussian fitting and model selection
experiments.variant: Herglotz localization with the same downstream fitting
experiments.loudness_matching: not applicable to detection; required only for later resynthesis listening
experiments.success: advantage survives manual or measured ground truth and tracking
experiments.cancel: ground truth is only ISM-derived or false positives and tracking failures erase the gain

experiments.title: Fixed versus adaptive FoV-BSM on real multi-source music capture
experiments.loudness_matching: retain raw cue and safety renders; separate binaural loudness-matched blind copies
experiments.success: adaptive advantage persists in real multi-source music without cue or timbre damage
experiments.cancel: source overlap, HRTF mismatch or motion removes the advantage or protected qualities worsen

handoff: Keep Herglotz and adaptive FoV as spatial-analysis research candidates, not rock-mix controls. Compare linked and unlinked parallel drum compression with the CLA chain fixed; preserve raw peak, mono and image checks, and judge preference only on separate loudness-matched blind copies. Treat all spoken settings as source-specific hypotheses and never auto-apply them.
